annotation.title_clean: Enhancing Linguist Productivity through Session-Logging and Data Pipelines; Ethical Challenges of Emotionally Intelligent AI in Humanoid Robots
annotation.title_en: Enhancing Linguist Productivity through Session-Logging and Data Pipelines; Ethical Challenges of Emotionally Intelligent AI in Humanoid Robots
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra Online Archive (BS thesis)
annotation.summary_en: Bachelor's thesis abstract combining a technical report on a Meta session-logging pipeline with an STS paper reviewing five studies on emotionally intelligent humanoid robots. It argues transparency alone is insufficient for vulnerable users and calls for binding regulation on psychological harms plus changes in engineer training.
key_provisions_or_claims: Transparency alone does not prevent emotional bonding with humanoid robots.
Greater transparency can reduce user trust in the system.
Existing ethical frameworks ignore commercial pressure to maximize engagement.
Binding regulation should hold organizations accountable for psychological harms.
Engineering education should change to consider the people affected by design choices.
